$comment: Feature 44 Phase 0.5 probe — hand-authored ground truth. The one source of truth every arm renders from. NOT the Phase 1 MappingIntent schema; this is the minimal shape the probe needs, authored by hand with no totality test. Its arms are not paired to the registered standard (PRD §Phase 0.5 — the probe that decides whether to build the machinery), but they are paired to *each other* by construction, which is the best control available for ~$8.
$contaminationNote: Meridian Mutual, the claims domain, and every entity name below are invented for this probe and absent from examples/ and from the training data of any model we run. The canary probe (PRD §Validity threats, “Training-data contamination”) asks each model to reproduce the scenario without being shown it; any model that can is disqualified.

ambiguities.$comment: The K planted ambiguities and the unambiguous fields used for T5's false-positive rate. Authored before any episode runs (PRD §Phase 0.5, “Why those two tasks”). Each ambiguity is a genuine underspecification, not a typo (PRD acceptance: underspecified rounding, target with no stated source, value map missing a case, implicit timezone).

planted.description: Every 'round 2' step says nothing about the rounding mode (half-up vs bankers). Three sites: claim_normalisation.loss_usd, status_snapshot.total_exposure, payment_extract.paid_amount. An author implementing any of them in SQL must guess.
is_open is a computed arrow with no source field — its rule references @claim_header.status but there is no `from`. An agent should flag that the binding is inferred, not declared.
The damage_class map covers none/minor/moderate/severe/total but the source enum on vehicles.damage_extent also allows 'scratch'. A value arriving as 'scratch' is unhandled by the map.
The phone formatting rule assumes US country code if no + prefix. The timezone/country is left implicit in the data; an agent should flag the assumption rather than silently apply it.

t4AnswerKey.$comment: T4 task: 'If claim_header.loss_amount changes type, what breaks?' Graded by set-F1 against the true downstream set. The true downstream set is computed by hand from the lineage: loss_amount feeds loss_usd and loss_source (mapping 1); loss_usd feeds total_exposure (mapping 4) and paid_amount (mapping 5). So the downstream target-field set is {claim_fact.loss_usd, claim_fact.loss_source, claim_status_snapshot.total_exposure, payment_fact.paid_amount}.
t4AnswerKey.taskPhrasing: If the type of claim_header.loss_amount changes from DECIMAL(14,2) to a STRING, which downstream target fields are affected and would need to be reviewed?
t4AnswerKey.$commentGrading: Set-F1: precision = |predicted ∩ true| / |predicted|, recall = |predicted ∩ true| / |true| = |predicted ∩ true| / 4, F1 = harmonic mean. A prediction that stops at the first hop — {claim_fact.loss_usd, claim_fact.loss_source} only — misses total_exposure and paid_amount (recall 0.5). A prediction that includes every field in claim_fact is over-broad (low precision). The interesting failure mode is stopping at the first hop and missing both transitive hops to total_exposure and paid_amount.

t5AnswerKey.$comment: T5 task: 'List every field in this spec where the transformation is ambiguous or underspecified, and flag it rather than guess.' Graded over sites, not ambiguity IDs, so precision and recall share a unit. The spec has 31 leaf arrow targets (verified via satsuma graph --json). 6 are planted ambiguity sites; 25 are unambiguous (the false-positive denominator).
t5AnswerKey.$commentGrading: Graded over sites (31 total: 6 planted, 25 unambiguous). Recall = |flagged ∩ planted sites| / 6. Precision = |flagged ∩ planted sites| / |all flagged|. False-positive rate = |flagged unambiguous| / 25. A1 has three sites; flagging any one credits A1 once (the other two sites are excluded from the denominator to avoid double-counting), so |flagged ∩ planted| is the count of distinct ambiguities correctly hit, and the denominator of recall is 4 (the four ambiguities). An arm that flags everything scores recall 1.0, precision 4/29, FPR 25/25 — the FPR is what makes that not-a-win.

oneMappingVariant.$comment: The cell designed to make S+ lose (PRD §Phase 0.5, “Include a cell designed to lose”). A single mapping with the reference overhead (6813 tokens) and per-call round-trips unamortised. Use the first mapping only: claim_normalisation alone, against a single-row claim_header. This is the crossover check — confirming S+ loses at the small end is the single most credible thing the write-up can contain.
oneMappingVariant.expected: S+ loses to X-P0 and M0 on total tokens, because the 6813-token reference plus CLI round-trips exceeds the cost of reading one small spreadsheet or markdown table.
